topics.title: The invisible man: words about seeing

learn.hook: Imagine footprints appearing on a London street with nobody standing in them!
points: 'Footprints without Feet' by H.G. Wells is about Griffin, a brilliant scientist who makes his body invisible by swallowing certain rare drugs.
Two boys in London are amazed to see fresh muddy footprints appear on the steps with no one there.
Griffin finds being invisible far from easy: he must stay unclothed to be unseen, so he feels cold and has to find clothes and shelter. He soon turns to wrongdoing.
Vocabulary: transparent (clearly see-through), translucent (lets some light through, not clearly), opaque (lets no light through), invisible (cannot be seen).
The prefix in- often means 'not': invisible, incorrect, incomplete.

example.q: Passage: The new glass door at the mall was so clean and transparent that Bunty walked straight into it. He rubbed his nose while his sister giggled behind him. Why did Bunty walk into the door?
steps: It was transparent, so light passed through it and he could see straight through.
He did not notice it was there.
example.answer: The door was so transparent that he did not see it.

learn.reallife: Science-fiction ideas inspire real research, such as 'invisibility cloaks' that bend light in labs, though nothing like Griffin's has been made.

quiz.explain: It is adapted from H.G. Wells's 'The Invisible Man'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up authors of Footprints without Feet

options: A scientist who made himself invisible
quiz.explain: Griffin is the scientist whose experiment made him invisible.

options: By drinking a lot of water
quiz.explain: He swallowed rare drugs that made his body transparent.
quiz.mistake: Uses fantasy ideas from other stories

quiz.q: What did the two boys in London see?
options: A ghost in a white sheet
Fresh muddy footprints with no one there
quiz.explain: They saw footprints appearing on the steps without anyone visible.
quiz.mistake: Adds dramatic events not in the lesson

quiz.explain: Transparent things, like clear glass, let us see through them.
Opaque objects, like wood, block light completely.

quiz.q: What does the prefix 'in-' mean in 'invisible'?
Passage: The new glass door at the mall was so clean and transparent that Bunty walked straight into it. He rubbed his nose while his sister giggled behind him. Why did Bunty walk into the door?
options: He was looking at his phone
It was so transparent that he did not see it
quiz.explain: The passage links the clean, transparent glass with his bump.

teach.ask: Gappu: If you can see through glass, is glass invisible? What's the difference between transparent and invisible?
teach.praise: Peek-a-chirp! Transparent lets light through; invisible means you can't see it at all. Griffin was invisible!
teach.nudge: Does transparent mean you cannot see the thing, or that you can see through it?

topics.title: Science and ethics: letter to the editor

learn.hook: If you could become invisible, would you use it for good? Griffin's answer is a warning.
points: Griffin misuses his discovery: instead of sharing it for good, he uses invisibility to steal and frighten people.
The story raises a question of ethics (moral principles of right and wrong): a great discovery needs responsibility.

A letter to the editor gives your views on a public issue. Format: sender's address, date, receiver's address, subject, salutation (Sir/Madam), body, complimentary close (Yours faithfully), signature and name.
The body: introduce the issue, give reasons and examples, suggest solutions, and close politely.
Keep the tone formal, polite and to the point; avoid slang and personal attacks.

example.q: Write a suitable subject line for a letter to the editor about people flying drones over a crowded festival ground.
steps: A subject line is short and states the issue clearly.
Name the problem: unsafe drone flying.
Name the place or event: crowded festival grounds.
example.answer: Subject: Unsafe flying of drones over crowded festival grounds

learn.reallife: Letters to the editor in newspapers let citizens raise issues like noise, traffic, cleanliness or the safe use of technology.

games.title: Ethics and letter check
items: Griffin uses his invisibility to help people.
He uses it to steal and frighten people.
Ethics means moral principles of right and wrong.
Ethics guides how we should act.
A letter to the editor should be formal and polite.
It is a formal letter to a newspaper.
'Your loving friend' is a good closing for a letter to the editor.
'Yours faithfully' or 'Yours truly' is used in formal letters.
The subject line comes just before the salutation.
It sums up the issue before 'Sir/Madam'.
A letter to the editor should only complain and never suggest solutions.

quiz.q: What is the central message of 'Footprints without Feet'?
options: A great scientific discovery can be harmful if used without ethics
quiz.explain: Griffin's misuse of his discovery shows the need for responsibility.
quiz.mistake: Reads the story as just an adventure

quiz.q: How does Griffin misuse his invisibility?
options: He uses it to cure diseases
He uses it to steal and frighten people
He uses it to win races
quiz.explain: He becomes a lawless man who robs and scares people.
quiz.mistake: Assumes a scientist would use a discovery for good

options: Moral principles of right and wrong
Good manners at the dinner table
quiz.explain: Ethics deals with what is morally right or wrong.

quiz.q: Which complimentary close suits a letter to the editor?
quiz.explain: Formal letters to editors end with 'Yours faithfully' (or 'Yours truly').

quiz.q: In a formal letter, what comes immediately before the salutation?
quiz.explain: The order is: receiver's address, subject, salutation.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parts of the format

quiz.q: Which salutation is right for a letter to the editor?
Which is the best subject line for a letter to the editor?
options: Subject: Loudspeakers played late at night in residential areas
quiz.explain: It is short, clear and names the issue.
quiz.mistake: Writes a vague or emotional subject

quiz.q: What tone should a letter to the editor have?
quiz.explain: Even when complaining, the tone stays formal and respectful.
quiz.mistake: Thinks strong feelings need rude language

teach.ask: Gappu: If I invented an invisibility potion, what should I think about? And how do I write to the newspaper about it?
teach.praise: Responsible-chirp! Science needs ethics, and my letter will be formal, with a subject and 'Yours faithfully'.
teach.nudge: Should a discovery be used responsibly? And which parts make a letter formal?
